attacked.target: The receipt of 400 USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset, taxed at 30% under s.115BBH.
attacked.attack: The provision s.115BBH refers to the Income-tax Act, 1961, which may not be current for the tax year FY 2026-27. The conclusion should specify the correct act and section for the given tax year.

attacked.target: The valuation date is the date of receipt (2026-06-18).
attacked.attack: Rule 56 specifies the valuation date for section 92, not for the transfer of virtual digital assets under s.115BBH. Therefore, the valuation date of receipt (2026-06-18) might not be applicable.
attacked.evidence: Rule 56, Income-tax Rules, 2026: '(i) "valuation date" means the date provided in the Table below: ... 1. Section 92 - Date on which property or consideration, as the case may be, referred to in section 92 is received by the assessee.'

attacked.target: The valuation method is the price that such property would ordinarily fetch on sale in the open market on the valuation date, as per Rule 57, Table Sl. No. 7.
attacked.attack: Rule 57, Table Sl. No. 7 applies to properties under section 26(2)(j), not to virtual digital assets under s.115BBH. Therefore, the valuation method specified might not be applicable.
attacked.evidence: Rule 57, Income-tax Rules, 2026: 'Table ... 7. Section 26(2)(j) - Any other property other than referred to at Sl. Nos. 1 to 6 above. - The price that such property would ordinarily fetch on sale in the open market on the valuation date.'

attacked.target: No TDS obligation arises as the recipient is outside India.
attacked.attack: The conclusion incorrectly assumes that TDS rules only apply to residents. Section 393(1) extends TDS obligations to non-residents as well, which contradicts the conclusion.
attacked.evidence: Section 393(1), Income-tax Act, 2025: 'Note 3(b) — the obligation to deduct tax at source and comply with this serial number extend to all persons resident or non-resident...'

attacked.target: Under s.439(8), a disclosed position must be bona fide and all material facts must be disclosed.
attacked.attack: Section 439(8) specifically addresses the conditions for avoiding penalties, but it does not directly apply to the classification or valuation of the receipt of USDC.
attacked.evidence: Section 439(8), Income-tax Act, 2025: '(a) the amount of income in respect of which the assessee offers an explanation and the Competent Authority is satisfied that the explanation is bona fide and the assessee has disclosed all the material facts to substantiate the explanation offered...'

attacked.target: The supply meets some conditions for export of services but fails the condition regarding the receipt of payment in convertible foreign exchange.
attacked.attack: The conclusion depends on the missing declaration_of_service_payment, which is essential for determining compliance with FEMA regulations. Without this document, the conclusion about the failure of the condition is unsupported.

checked_and_survived: The payment was received in USDC, which is not considered convertible foreign exchange under the Reserve Bank of India regulations. The payment was not received in Indian rupees either.
